data.name: The Captives: Plot of the Demiurge
data.detailed_description:
Characters

The Captives: Plot of the Demiurge is an action-adventure game with a variety of carefully crafted levels. You will start by creating your character for each particular level. You can customize the character’s name, stats, weapon and appearance, giving each character you play a unique feel.


After each level your personalized character gets added to the story’s cast of NPCs whom you can then talk to and interact with. As the story grows, so too does your cast of previous player characters.

Setting

The Captives: Plot of the Demiurge is set during a struggle between two opposing ideologies. After Prince Pico and the city-state of Volturno leave the anti-magic Tetrarchy to explore the alluring possibilities of the magic sciences, the other states band together to retake Volturno and stop whatever scheme Pico may have begun with his newly-acquired arcane knowledge...

Story

You play as convicted prisoners, drafted into the Tetrarch’s army to undertake missions against Prince Pico’s forces and collect intelligence concerning his masterplan. While each prisoner has their own individual personality and backstory, all share one goal: to complete their assigned objectives and earn their freedom.

Customization

When you create your character you will choose from a variety of weapons and distribute your skill points amongst four stats. Since your available skill points are limited, you will have to think carefully about how you invest them.

The four stats of the Captives are:

  • Health
    Health helps your character survive damage – pretty straight forward! A character with lots of health will allow you more room for mistakes while a character with little health will have to be more careful to avoid damage.

  • Stamina
    Stamina is used for each action in the game: attacking, defending and dodging. A character with lots of stamina will be able to chain together many attacks while a character with little stamina will have to be more tactical and patient.

  • Focus
    Focus prevents your character from being staggered by enemy attacks. A character with lots of focus will be able to shrug off damage while swinging away at enemies while a character with little focus should try to fight enemies one at a time.

  • Movement
    Movement determines the speed at which your character moves. A character with a lot of movement will be able to dance around their foes while a character with little movement will have to time their aggression carefully.

Playstyle

All the numbers in The Captives are very low so that the difference between spending a single stat point in health over movement can change the feel of how your character plays significantly.


It’s not possible to create a character that is good at everything. Because you will play as multiple characters you can experiment with different weapons and stats and explore what the combat has to offer within a single playthrough, instead of being locked into one playstyle for the entire game.

Combat

The combat of The Captives is real-time tactical action in the style of the Zelda or Souls games. Anticipation and timing is a consistent key to success, although each character you create will require different approaches depending on how you invested your skill points.


Gameplay Modifiers

Replay the game with special Challenge Runs, combinations of unique modifiers to the game.

These include Roguelike Challenge which randomises your build each time you play through the dungeons and Soul Challenge which restricts the number of checkpoints in the game and changes how healing works.

With a variety of individual modifiers you can also tweak the game to create your own challenge runs or make things a little easier if you get stuck.

When does this game release?

October 11th 2018

data.short_description: The Captives: Plot of the Demiurge is an action-adventure game with real-time combat. Play as ten different characters of your creation. At the end of playing as one character they become an NPC! Assemble your own collection of prisoners and work together to defeat the evil schemes of Prince Pico.

reviews.review:
[h1] In A Nutshell [/h1]

🔵 [b] Pros [/b]
+ Plenty of alternative game modes and custom modifiers.
+ Decent storyline coated with humor.
+ Good character progression system with interesting mechanics.
+ Some challenging boss fights and encounters.

🔴 [b] Cons [/b]
- Unbalanced, bizarre stamina management system.
- Multiple weapon balance issues derived from the problem above.
- Inability to change weapons once a level is started.
- Several mechanics are not used at their full potential.

The Captives is essentially top-down a dungeon crawler featuring ten different characters for the same amount of stages. Each of these characters can be customized in attributes, weapons, appearance, and once the stage is completed, you may meet that character again in future ones as a companion. This mechanic is however used only in a few levels and just seems a large waste of potential. 

Combat is promoted as "souls-like", but the only similarities with the Souls series are the dodge mechanic, back-stabs and perfect parrying. Enemies do not give any experience, as leveling up is done via several "crates" found around each level, giving one Attribute Point each time to spend; Six are present in each level, often behind hidden places or additional dangerous areas. Checkpoints do not offer any function besides re-spawn point, and there are no different weapons or pieces of gear ti drop from defeated enemies.

Level design gets pretty intricate in the last few levels, while being normal or simple in the other stages. There are unlock-able shortcuts to access later stage areas more easily, secret levers and keys to find to open secondary areas probably containing Attribute Chests. Besides this, there isn't much left in levels, the occasional NPCs with some lines of dialogue may shed some light on the lore and storyline, while rarely some of your former characters may join you as companions.

Overall, The Captives is a decent top-down hack and slash, but some of its mechanics and design choices result to be detrimental and hold it back from being a truly good game.

[quote]Liked this review, and want to see more of the same quality? Check out [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/39323490]Tamaster's Review Archive[/url] to see all my Reviews in a single, convenient location.[/quote]

[h1] In-depth Feature Analysis [/h1]


🎮 [b] Gameplay [/b]
The gameplay of The Captives is divided mainly into Preparation, Exploration and Combat.

The character preparation screen features a complete appearance editor, where you can choose face, clothes and details of your hero. Armors and such are only cosmetic and have no impact in gameplay. This part will also allow choosing from different weapons ranging from nimble daggers to massive halberds, of course each having different damage values, attack speed, patterns, and stagger values. Lastly, you will be able to put six attribute points into one of the four available ones: Health, Stamina, Focus and Speed to best suit your character build. Accurate descriptions of what each attribute does and what special effects it delivers are present.

Exploration of dungeons will feature various rooms, each of them being a stand-alone fight featuring one or more enemies, when a room is cleared, your Health is completely restored, this is the only form of healing in the game aside from Checkpoints, who also reset all enemies like in souls-like games. Additional areas can often be unlocked with levers or keys found while exploring, and often lead to Attribute Crates, giving one Point to spend in any statistic you want to improve the character. Always six of them are present in each stage and this is the only "leveling-up" available. No other items are present to loot or discover aside from Keys and Crates.


📖 [b] Story [/b]
The story of The Captives starts of seeming pretty serious, but soon become coated with humor, with an alternation of serious and funny moments. Do not expect a very serious and accurate depiction of characters, as each of them will be likely oriented to be comedic and funny rather than serious. It's not bad by any means even if it's a bit of a cliche and just does not shine a lot for originality or complexity.


👊 [b] Combat System [/b]
Combat takes a lot of inspiration from the famous Souls series, but is not, by a long shot, as difficult or complex as that, think of it as a quite watered down version. It is based mostly on dodging at the right times, understanding enemy attack patterns, circle around foes to backstab, and eventually also parry at the right time to counter attack.

The biggest issue of an otherwise good system is how Stamina is managed: every light attack of any weapon costs one stamina while heavy costs two. This means a greatsword inflicting great damage and a dagger have the same stamina cost, and also make no effect on the player's move speed. This makes heavier weapons completely overpowered while penalizing a lot lighter ones, effectively making only Halberds and Greatswords good weapons.

Also, the time window for a perfect parry is insanely small, much smaller than any Dark Souls game even, making it almost impossible to perform a perfect parry and stun the enemy.


💰 [b] Content & Pricing [/b]
Base price tag is 14€, offering about 9-12 hours of content for the main campaign, depending a lot on difficulty and skill level. Additional challenge modes can alter considerably the gameplay, offering some form of replay-ability to the most dedicated players, but don't expect a whole new gameplay from any of them. I'd say the game is worth it at this price for what it offers, even with the described issues.


🔗 [b] Balance & Challenge [/b]
Balance of weapons is way offset because of how stamina is managed, favoring heavier weapons a lot. Lighter weapons may be quicker but the damage output of heavier ones just is so much better. Enemies are mostly balanced except for two bosses I found to be very unbalanced and unfair, but not impossible.


[h1] Technical Analysis [/h1]


🎥 [b] Graphics [/b]
Graphics are pleasant but still pretty basic. Dynamic shadows are a good touch. Animations are fluid and well made, while effects are very basic. Model quality is pretty good. Texture quality is average for this type of game.


🔊 [b] Sound [/b]
Sound effects are pretty average, while soundtracks impressed me positively on some occasions.


🔩 [b] Performance & Stability [/b]
GPU usage is pretty on the heavy side because of Unity engine having optimization issues, a common problem with Unity games nowadays. Game otherwise runs well and has a complete set of options to tweak performance. [GTX1080, i7 4820K, 16GB RAM]


💻 [b] Artificial Intelligence [/b]
Enemy Ai, as expected, has a pattern based attack motion, but is also smart enough to avoid traps or bait you into more of their allies when alone. Pretty good.


🏠 [b] Quality of Life [/b]
One critical issue is present: it is not possible to change weapons once a level is started, while the autosave-only function prevents reloading. This means if you choose the wrong weapon for some situation or level, you will have a very very hard time, possibly making the run impossible. I personally was forced to restart the game because of this, as my weapon was just too bad and could not change it.


🐛 [b] Bugs & Issues [/b]
Sometimes heavier weapons will clip inside enemies when attacking and just not register the hit, if the enemy is doing as well an attack animation. This is rare but can happen.


[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
The Captives is quite a decent game and could be outright good if not for the few but serious design problems with STamina and Weapon Changing, which can botch entire runs and make the experience much less enjoyable. Still, it's a pretty good indie title you should check out.


This product was reviewed using a free key provided by the Developers.
